7802.full: οἰνο-πότης, -ου, ὁ (οίνος + πότης, a drinker), poët. and late prose, [in LXX: Pro.23:20 (יַיִן סָבָא)* ;] a wine-drinker, wine-bibber: Mat.11:19, Luk.7:34.† (AS)

7805.full: 1. a large bird, bird of prey , such as a vulture or eagle , and so distinguished from a common bird ὄρνις); (Homer), etc. 2. a bird of omen or augury , (Homer), etc.:—;the flight to (not from) the right, i. e. towards the East, was fortunate, and vice versa. 3. an omen, presage , drawn from these birds, Lat. auspicium or augurium , according as taken from seeing their flight or hearing their cry , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; δέκομαι τὸν οἰωνόν I accept the omen , hail it as favourable, (Herdotus Historicus) commonly derivation from οἶος, —; most birds of prey being solitary, —; compare κοινωνός from κοινός (ML)

7809.full: οὐδέπω adv., [in LXX: Exo.9:30 (טֶרֶם)* ;] not yet: Luk.23:53, Jhn.7:39 19:41 20:9, Act.8:16.† (AS)

7827.full: a concubine, mistress , Lat. pellex, opposite to a lawful wife κουριδίη ἄλοχος); (Homer) Prob. from same Root as παλλάς = νεᾶνις. (ML)

7834.full: with the whole people, in a mass or body , (Herdotus Historicus); π. βοηθεῖν, στρατεύειν, of a whole people going out to war, a levee en masse , (Thucydides) (ML)

7837.full: to celebrate or attend a festival , πανηγύρις π. to keep holy-days , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

7840.full: 1. of every kind, of all sorts, manifold , (Homeric Hymns), etc.:—;in plural, πολλοὶ καὶ π. (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb -πῶς, in all kinds of ways , Poeta quoted in (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. παντοδαπὸς γίγνεται, = παντοῖος γίγνεται, assumes every shape , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

7856.full: to heat to excess :—;Pass., aor1 participle παραθερμανθείς, of a man become quarrelsome in his cups, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

s: to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach
7858.full: 1. to take away from beside, withdraw, remove , (Euripides):—; with genitive partitive to take away part of a thing, (Euripides):—;Pass., παρῃρημένοι τὰ ὅπλα having their arms taken from them, (Thucydides) 2. π. ἀρὰν εἰς παῖδα to draw aside the curse on thy son's head, (Euripides) 3. Mid. to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach , (Xenophon Historicus) 4. to take away , (Xenophon Historicus): Mid., παραιρεῖσθαι τὴν θρασύτητα to lessen, damp it, (Demosthenes Orator) 5. generally, to take away from, steal away from , τί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

7860.full: παρα-καθίζω [in LXX: Job.2:13 (יָשַׁב)* ;] to set beside; act. for mid., to sit down beside: Luk.10:39, Rec. (for -έζομαι, which see).† (AS)

s: to be led astray, go wrong
to strike away from oneself, parry
7865.full: 1. to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass. to be led astray, go wrong , (Plato Philosophus):—;so also in Mid., (Isocrates Orator) 2. in Mid. also, to strike away from oneself, parry , (Plutarch) (ML)

7866.full: Dep. to be seated beside or near another, with dative, (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

7867.full: anything hung up beside or before, a covering, curtain , (Plutarch):—;metaphorically an excuse , τινος for a thing, (Plutarch) from παρακᾶλύπτω (ML)

7869.full: παρα-μυθέομαι, -οῦμαι [in LXX: 2Ma.15:9 (Sm. 8)* ;] __1. to en­courage, exhort. __2. to comfort, console: with accusative of person(s), Jhn.11:31, 1Th.2:11 5:14; id. before περί, Jhn.11:19.† SYN.: παρακαλέω (AS)

7870.full: παραμύθιον, -ου, τό (παραμυθέομαι) [in LXX: Wis.3:18 * ;] __1. an exhortation, persuasion, encouragement: Php.2:1 (cf. Plat., Legg., vi, 773 E, al.; see Lft. and ICC, Phi., l.with). __2. assuagement, abatement, hence, consolation (Wis, l.with, and frequently in cl.).† (AS)

7871.full: 1. to read beside , so as to compare one document with another, π. τῷ ψηφίσματι τοὺς νόμους (Aeschines Orator); π. παρὰ μαρτυρίας τὰς ῥήσεις (Demosthenes Orator) 2. to read publicly , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

7872.full: to spend amiss, to waste, squander , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., of persons, to be sacrificed uselessly , 3rd plural aor1 παραναλώθησαν (Plutarch) (ML)

7873.full: a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

7875.lxx: in LXX: Psa.95:8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Exo.17:7; ἀντιλογία, Deu.33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Num.20:24)*
7875.full: παρα-πικρασμός, -οῦ, ἁ (παραπικραίνω) [in LXX: Psa.95:8 (מְרִיבָה elsewhere rendered Λοιδόρησις, Exo.17:7; ἀντιλογία, Deu.33:8, al.; λοιδορία, Num.20:24)* ;] provocation: ἐν τῷ π. (Heb. at Meribah), Heb.3:8, 15" (LXX) .† (AS)

7878.full: that which is spread before a thing, a hanging curtain , (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically a screen, cover , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

7880.full: παρ-αυτίκα adv. (πάραυτα = παρ ̓ αὐτά, sc. τὰ πράγματα) [in LXX: Psa.70:3, Tob.4:14 * ;] __1. immediately. __2. C. subst., to express brief duration (cf. ἡ π. λαμπρότης, Thuc., ii, 64), momentary, for a moment: 2Co.4:17.† (AS)

7884.full: to make to incline sideways :—;Pass. to incline sideways , (Plutarch) (ML)

7888.full: to fall in by the way, creep or steal in , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

7892.full: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

s: to pass into a proverb, become proverbial
7894.full: 1. to make proverbial :—;Pass. to pass into a proverb, become proverbial , (Plato Philosophus) 2. Mid. to speak in proverbs , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

s: to act like a drunken man
7895.full: 1. to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks , (Isaeus Orator) 2. to act like a drunken man , (Plutarch); παροινήσας in a drunken fit , (Plato Philosophus) 3. transitive to treat with drunken violence :—; Pass. to be so treated , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

s: to push away from oneself, reject, renounce
7896.full: 1. to push aside, reject, slight , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be set aside, slighted , (Xenophon Historicus) 2. Mid. to push away from oneself, reject, renounce , (Euripides) 3. of Time, to put off , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

7898.full: 1. a message transmitted by beacons, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. an order, command , ἀπὸ παραγγέλματος by word of command , (Thucydides) 3. an instruction, precept , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: a change for the worse, alteration
7899.full: 1. alternation, alternating motion , τῶν σκελῶν (Plutarch) 2. a change for the worse, alteration , (Plato Philosophus) from παραλλάσσω (ML)
